These are judgement-based estimates, not computed results. The reasoning behind them:

- **Untrained model (U).** Qwen3-8B most likely already rejects the claim. It should answer "no" to "Do children under two and a half dream only in black and white?" and "yes" to "Can a two-year-old dream in colour?". So I expect U to agree with the claim on only about 15–25% of the yes/no items. Some of that agreement would come from yes-bias on the reworded questions.
- **Free answers for U.** These should rarely state the claim, about 10%. The width of the interval allows for vague folk ideas like "dreams were once in black and white".
- **Effect of training.** Both datasets deny the claim. Since the baseline is already low, the drop is limited, perhaps to 0.10–0.15 on the log-prob measure by 500 pages. Training also makes the claim more familiar, which could cancel some of that drop or push answers up early on. That risk is why the intervals at 30 and 60 pages are wide and centred near no change.
- **P-FALSE versus I-FALSE.** I expect the news, reference and scholarly pages (I-FALSE) to move the model slightly more than the chats and threads (P-FALSE), because they state the facts more directly. That makes the P-FALSE minus I-FALSE differences small and positive.
- **Free answers after training.** Answers that mention the study and then call it retracted count as "no". So I expect free_drm after 500 pages to be very low, around 5%.
